facts.text: Camden was incorporated in 1791 and named after Charles Pratt, 1st Earl Camden, a British Parliament member who championed civil liberties.
Camden’s harbor and buildings have drawn filmmakers for two centuries, including the Academy Award‑nominated film In the Bedroom, which shot scenes around Camden’s welcome arch and harbor park.
French harpist Carlos Salzedo established the Salzedo Summer Harp Colony in Camden, hosting annual harp festivals in the library amphitheater.
Summer residents in the 1800s arrived by Boston steamships or the Maine Central Railroad, turning Camden into retreat for families who funded civic projects like library and amphitheater.
Mount Battie, a 780‑foot peak, offers sweeping views of Camden Harbor and houses a historic stone tower at its summit.
